summary.headline: Sai Parenterals Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR198 crore with 15% EBITDA margin; FY27 guided to INR750 crore revenue at 17% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: FY26 was the first year after listing and the Noumed Pharmaceuticals (Australia) acquisition, completed 12 November 2025, so consolidation covers only about 4.5 months. Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR198 crore, EBITDA INR29 crore (about 15%) and PAT INR13 crore (about 6.6%). Standalone FY26 revenue was about INR162 crore (up 30%), EBITDA about INR33 crore (about 21%) and PAT about INR17 crore (up 64%). Management framed FY27 as an investment year, with none of the INR440 crore capex expected to add revenue until FY28.

financial_highlights.value: INR319 crore (INR90 crore long-term, INR229 crore short-term)

segments.name: CDMO export business
segments.commentary: Management names it the first growth engine and top priority; over 50% of consolidated revenue comes from long-term supply contracts in regulated markets. FY26 approvals covered 88 dossiers across regulated and emerging markets.

segments.name: Noumed (Australia and New Zealand)
segments.commentary: Provides regulated-market access, relationships with pharmacy chains (Wesfarmers Health, EBOS Group) covering about 2,100 of 5,500 Australian pharmacies, and a private-label OTC portfolio. Noumed added 5 dossiers in Australia in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Branded formulations (domestic)
segments.commentary: Described as a stable operating base with growing domestic customer relationships; no separate figures were given on the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target INR750 crore with EBITDA margin of about 17%, from organic growth at Sai and Noumed, with no contribution from new capex.
FY27 revenue weighted to H2 (management cited roughly 40:60 H1:H2 split), with Q3 and Q4 heavier.
FY28 expected to be the year the full impact of investments shows; majority of capex operational and debt expected to decline from FY28.
Guidance for FY28 to be given at end of FY27 once molecule filings and approvals are clearer.
Noumed backward integration to start in Q4 FY27, with full integration in FY28; Sai to supply bulk tablets to the Australian facility by end of Q4 FY27.
Management expects the revenue and profit growth visibility to hold over the next three to four years.
capex_capacity: INR440 crore growth capex programme, all targeted for completion in FY27; none expected to add to FY27 financial performance.

India: about INR110-111 crore for capacity expansion and EU-GMP upgrades of two injectable plants, plus additional dosage forms at the Australia-approved plant, due by end of FY27; fully funded from IPO proceeds.
India R&D centre: about INR15 crore, funded from IPO proceeds, focused on formulation development and dossier creation.

Adelaide (Australia) expansion: total planned capex about AUD 53 million (about INR311 crore), with about AUD 20 million federal government grant; about AUD 40 million spent to date; balance from debt and internal accruals.
Noumed Australian plant: TGA commissioning under way; validation to start October-November 2026, solid dosage packing first, then liquids through Jan-Mar 2027; TGA licence expected by 31 March 2027.
demand_pricing: Management expects working capital needs of about 25-30% of incremental revenue, funded mainly by internal accruals and some debt.
Working capital cycle expected to improve as CDMO exports grow, given long-term contracts and shorter receivable cycles.
Pipeline: 67 dossiers under development at Sai, expected to be commercialised in FY27 and FY28; launch timelines cut from 18-24 months to 6-9 months using 451 IP dossiers acquired with Noumed.
Noumed currently outsources manufacturing to Indian CMOs; part of this volume is expected to move in-house from Q4 FY27.
Management did not disclose pricing or realisation figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated PBT fall despite revenue doubling year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: The analyst's question was answered on a standalone basis: standalone PBT was about INR18.85 crore in FY26 against INR14.4 crore in FY25. The consolidated PBT point was not addressed directly.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Noumed plant take to ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Clean rooms, HVAC, water systems and equipment are complete; validation starts October-November 2026, with solid dosage first and liquids through Jan-Mar 2027, and TGA licence expected by 31 March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top three strategic execution priorities?
qa_highlights.answer: In order: the CDMO export business; integration of Australia and New Zealand (Noumed) with Sai; and the branded formulations business as a stable base.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of planned and deployed capex in India and Australia?
qa_highlights.answer: India: about INR110 crore plus INR15 crore for R&D, funded from IPO proceeds. Australia: about AUD 53 million total, with about AUD 40 million already spent, balance from grant, debt and accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What incremental revenue will the capex generate in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: None. Management said capex completes by Q4 FY27 and benefits start in FY28-FY29; FY27 guidance excludes new capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide INR750 crore when Q4 annualises above INR750 crore, and how does margin rise from about 14.6% to 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is seasonal, with H2 heavier (about 40:60). Margin uplift is expected from shifting Noumed's outsourced products to Sai's manufacturing from Q4 FY27, with full integration in FY28. Management said guidance would be reviewed at the next results.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deferred tax credit in FY26 profit?
qa_highlights.answer: The tax line is negative for two reasons: recognition of a deferred tax asset, and a move from the old regime at 25% to the new regime at about 22%.

risks_watch: Execution risk on the Adelaide expansion, Noumed plant TGA licence (targeted by 31 March 2027) and EU-GMP upgrades, all due in FY27.
FY27 is a peak-debt year (total debt INR319 crore at March 2026); watch whether debt falls from FY28 as guided.
Seasonality and H2 weighting: Q4 FY26 margin of about 15% is below the 17% FY27 target.
Guidance is only for FY27; FY28 guidance deferred to end of FY27.
Working capital needs of 25-30% of incremental revenue could pressure cash flow.
Analyst questions on consolidated PBT and tax credit were answered only partly on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the strategy and the FY28 payoff, but cautious on near-term numbers: FY27 revenue guidance is described as conservative and FY27 is called an investment year. Answers on margin bridge and the tax credit were brief and partly generalised.
key_quotes: Importantly, none of the ongoing capex projects, the INR440 crores capex program are expected to contribute to FY 127 financial performance, as most of these facilities will be commissioned towards the end of the year.
We will move from a phase of building assets to a phase of monetizing them.
